records.question: How does uncertainty in data affect standard quadratic optimization problems?

In that paradigm, the decision-maker has to decide upon an uncertainty set $\mathcal{U}$ which encapsulates all the known information about the uncertain parameter.
The uncertain parameter (in this case the uncertain data matrix Q ) is supposed to reside within the uncertainty set $\mathcal{U}$, as violations are not allowed [10].
The uncertain matrix Q consisted of a nominal part $\mathrm{Q}^{(\text {nom })}$ and an uncertain additive perturbation $U$.

$$

$$

where the uncertain matrix $\tilde{\mathbf{Q}}$ is replaced by its expectation $\mathbb{E}[\tilde{\mathbf{Q}}]$.

records.question: What is the standard quadratic optimization problem (StQP) and why is it significant?
records.expected_answer: The standard quadratic optimization problem (StQP) involves minimizing a quadratic form over the standard simplex, which is a set of linear constraints. It is significant because it represents one of the simplest non-convex objective functions and can model various complex problems, such as portfolio optimization and maximum clique problems. Despite its simplicity, StQP can be NP-hard without specific assumptions on the matrix involved.

evidence.text:
## 1 Introduction

The standard quadratic optimization problem (StQP) consists of minimizing a quadratic form over the standard simplex

$$
\ell(\mathrm{Q}):=\min _{\mathbf{x} \in \Delta} \mathbf{x}^{\top} \mathrm{Q} \mathbf{x}
$$

where $\mathrm{Q} \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$ is a symmetric matrix, and $\Delta:=\left\{\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^{n}: \mathbf{e}^{\top} \mathbf{x}=1, \mathbf{x} \geq \mathbf{0}\right\}$ is the standard simplex in $\mathbb{R}^{n}$.
it is NP-hard without assumptions on the definiteness of the matrix Q.
